Archaeologists in Egypt have uncovered a well-preserved Byzantine-era city in the western desert.

The fourth-century quarters had residential and religious structures, including a basilica-style church in the Dakhla oasis. Archaeologists also found coins, pottery fragments and tools.

rfi.description: Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said Wednesday that Greenland was "not for sale" following remarks by President Donald Trump suggesting the territory should be controlled by Washington and not Copenhagen.

rfi.title: Oil prices continue to rally as US and Iran step up mutual attacks
rfi.description: Oil prices jumped more than 3 percent on Wednesday as the Middle East crisis burst back into the spotlight, with United States and Iranian forces exchanging strikes after attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, fuelling fresh supply fears.

rfi.title: Switzerland beat Colombia on penalties to set up last-eight date with Argentina
rfi.description: Switzerland beat Colombia in a penalty shootout on Tuesday to advance to the last eight at the World Cup for the first time since 1954. They will play Argentina on Saturday in Kansas City.

rfi.title: Le Pen confirms  presidential bid after Paris appeals court upholds conviction
rfi.description: The leader of France's far-right National Rally, Marine Le Pen, said on Tuesday she would run for president next year after an embezzlement conviction was confirmed on appeal, a ruling she said she would challenge before the country's highest court.

rfi.title: Climate justice in Africa: floods, fossil fuels and the fightback
rfi.description: This week in Spotlight on Africa, we look at climate change, environmental justice and the challenges of adaptation. While Europe's heatwaves make headlines, temperatures are also climbing across Africa, with parts of the Sahel approaching 50°C. West Africa is also experiencing severe flooding caused by climate change. Yet Africa is also a source of innovation and solutions, as we'll be discussing today.

rfi.title: Macron condemns Paraguayan senator's racist remarks as Mbappé hits back
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé condemned a Paraguayan senator on Monday for making racist comments about him following France's World Cup victory over Paraguay, calling her "despicable" and "not worthy" of her position.

rfi.title: Argentina return from the brink to beat Egypt and reach World Cup quarter-finals
rfi.description: Argentina advanced to the last eight at the World Cup after recovering from a two-goal deficit to see off Egypt 3-2 on Tuesday.

rfi.description: The European Commission has warned that a French bill that would ban children under the age of 15 from social media would infringe the European Union’s online content law by giving French regulators powers that go beyond the bloc’s legal framework.

rfi.title: NATO summit in Ankara tests unity as Ukraine war and Trump tensions loom
rfi.description: As NATO leaders gather in Ankara tomorrow, Tuesday, the alliance faces a stark test of unity, burden-sharing and strategic clarity, with the war in Ukraine, transatlantic tensions and Middle East instability all pressing heavily on the agenda.

rfi.title: France's first diagnosed Ebola patient recovers after treatment
rfi.description: A French doctor who was the first-ever diagnosed case of Ebola in the country has made a full recovery and has been discharged from hospital.

rfi.description: Firefighters are fighting wildfires across southern France and other parts of Europe, and authorities are warning that this year’s fire season has started a month earlier than usual after early heatwaves in May and June left vegetation particularly dry and vulnerable.

euronews.title: Trump tempers fury with allies and ends 'tremendously successful' NATO summit on high note
euronews.description: European leaders showcased their surging defence spending at the summit as they looked to convince Trump they're making good on a pledge to ramp up budgets and take more responsibility for their own security.

euronews.title: 'Associating Islam with violence contradicts its true nature': Global Forum debates Islamic heritage

euronews.description: Experts say human-caused climate change is intensifying South Asia’s monsoons, which traditionally run from June to September and again from October to December.

euronews.description: Scientists are questioning whether FIFA's hydration breaks do enough to protect players competing in extreme heat. While some argue the breaks disrupt the game, researchers say longer cooling periods and active cooling measures may better reduce heat-related health risks.

euronews.description: The European Union is set to revise its Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) to cover non-EU issuers and broaden its scope, as US President Donald Trump's support for stablecoins prompts new regulatory questions.

lemonde.title: En Europe, la crainte du retour de l’Allemagne comme puissance militaire
lemonde.description: En prévoyant de consacrer 3,5 % de son produit intérieur brut à sa défense d’ici à 2029, Berlin répond aux attentes de ses alliés, qui somment le pays depuis des années de prendre davantage ses responsabilités sur la scène internationale. Mais ce réarmement ravive de vieilles peurs, notamment en France, en Italie et en Pologne.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Marine Le Pen abrège un premier déplacement de campagne chahuté
lemonde.description: Au lendemain de sa condamnation par la cour d’appel de Paris, la cheffe de file de l’extrême droite a écourté, mercredi, sa venue à La Flèche, dans la Sarthe, perturbée par la mobilisation d’une soixantaine d’opposants.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : les Etats-Unis pourraient frapper l’Iran « plus en profondeur » dans la nuit, selon Pete Hegseth, le secrétaire d’Etat à la défense
lemonde.description: Donald Trump avait menacé un peu plus tôt, mercredi, de détruire des infrastructures civiles iraniennes et de « prendre le contrôle de l’île de Kharg ».  Les bombardements ont repris durant la nuit de mardi à mercredi dans le Golfe, alors que se tient un sommet de l’OTAN en Turquie.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, canicule : des records de chaleur enregistrés dans plusieurs stations du sud de la France, jusqu’à 43 °C relevés dans l’Hérault
lemonde.description: Des températures supérieures à 40 °C ont été également atteintes dans les Bouches-du-Rhône, dans le Gard et dans les Pyrénées-Orientales. Par ailleurs, avec une chaleur qui gagne du terrain et des vents renforcés, l’alerte incendies reste maximale sur une partie du pourtour méditerranéen.

lemonde.title: Scission de Vivendi : Vincent Bolloré gagne encore une manche face aux actionnaires minoritaires
lemonde.description: La cour d’appel de Paris a donné gain de cause, mercredi, au groupe breton, premier actionnaire du conglomérat, à qui le fonds CIAM demandait de lancer une offre publique de retrait. Le fonds va se pourvoir en cassation.

lemonde.title: France-Maroc : la soif de revanche des Lions de l’Atlas, quatre ans après la demi-finale perdue au Qatar
lemonde.description: La sélection marocaine de football n’a battu la France qu’une seule fois, lors d’un tournoi amical, en mai 1998. Vingt-huit ans plus tard, ses supporteurs ont des raisons de croire en une victoire de leur équipe, plus forte que jamais, en quarts de finale du Mondial 2026.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : le gouvernement russe interdit les exportations de gazole en raison des pénuries provoquées par les frappes ukrainiennes
lemonde.description: Cette interdiction « est entrée en vigueur aujourd’hui [mercredi], ce qui permettra d’augmenter les approvisionnements sur le marché intérieur », a déclaré le vice-premier ministre russe, Alexandre Novak, lors d’une réunion avec Vladimir Poutine. De son côté, Donald Trump a annoncé que les Etats-Unis allaient autoriser les Ukrainiens à fabriquer des missiles Patriot.

lemonde.title: Fonction publique : le gouvernement exclut une hausse générale des salaires mais promet des dispositifs ciblés
lemonde.description: Le ministre de l’action et des comptes publics, David Amiel, a présidé mercredi 8 juillet un « rendez-vous salarial » avec les employeurs publics et les organisations syndicales. Les représentants du personnel – qui ont quitté la réunion — dénoncent un « acte manqué ».

lemonde.title: Emmy Awards : les séries « The Pitt » et « Hacks » en tête des nominations
lemonde.description: La cérémonie se tiendra le 14 septembre à Los Angeles, et sera présentée par Mariska Hargitay, actrice popularisée par la série « New York Unité spéciale ».

lemonde.title: « Sa prothèse lui fait mal, mais il supporte pour ne pas montrer qu’il est différent » : à Gaza, le traumatisme des enfants mutilés de guerre
lemonde.description: En raison des bombardements menés par Israël depuis le 7 octobre 2023, la bande de Gaza détient le triste record du plus grand nombre d’enfants amputés par habitant au monde, selon l’Organisation mondiale de la santé. Ces derniers tentent de se reconstruire malgré les déplacements forcés et la pénurie de soins dans un territoire en ruines.

lemonde.title: Déremboursement d’actes médicaux : inquiétude face à la piste d’une hausse du ticket modérateur
lemonde.description: Le projet d’augmenter la somme à la charge des patients, et prise en charge par les mutuelles, n’est pas encore confirmé, mais il apparaît comme la principale piste d’économies avancée par le gouvernement.

lemonde.title: « On peut se débarrasser de son stress ici » : à Oakland, loin de la Coupe du monde, le « pouvoir du football » au service des réfugiés
lemonde.description: L’organisation Soccer Without Borders est installée au sein d’un lycée de la ville californienne qui n’accueille que des migrants ou des réfugiés.

lemonde.title: Face à l’inflation, une proposition de loi veut instaurer un panier de produits sains à prix coûtant
lemonde.description: Dans le sillage du rapport de la commission d’enquête du Sénat sur les marges, Boris Tavernier, député écologiste de la 2ᵉ circonscription du Rhône, a déposé, mercredi, une proposition de loi visant à garantir au sein des grands distributeurs l’accès à un panier de produits alimentaires sains et diversifiés vendus sans marge.

lemonde.title: Des chercheurs ont pu observer en direct l’expansion d’une dorsale océanique
lemonde.description: Grâce à des instruments de mesure placés à près de 2 000 mètres de profondeur, au large de l’île Amsterdam, une équipe française a pu suivre ce phénomène, le 26 avril 2024. Les géophysiciens ont constaté que le plancher abyssal s’était étendu en quelques jours de 2 à 4 mètres.

lemonde.title: Justice criminelle : députés et sénateurs s’accordent sur le projet de loi de Gérald Darmanin
lemonde.description: Sauf surprise, le projet de loi, expurgé de plusieurs mesures clivantes, dont le « plaider-coupable », devrait désormais être adopté sans encombre, la gauche étant la seule à s’y opposer à l’Assemblée.

lemonde.title: Tour de France : Olav Kooij s’impose au sprint, Torstein Traeen conserve le maillot jaune malgré une chute dans le final
lemonde.description: Le sprinteur de la Decathlon-CMA CGM s’est imposé au sprint final, mercredi à Pau, lors de la cinquième étape du Tour de France 2026. Le Français Baptiste Veistroffer, échappé depuis le départ, a été rattrapé à dix kilomètres de l’arrivée.

france24fr.title: Élevages décimés, récoltes réduites : l'agriculture forcée de s'adapter aux canicules ?
france24fr.description: Des millions de volailles mortes de chaud, un risque accru d’incendie pendant les moissons, des fruits cuits sur pied… Depuis dimanche 5 juillet, la France est traversée par une nouvelle vague de chaleur, la troisième, déjà, depuis le début de la canicule mi-mai. Ces épisodes précoces et rapprochés fragilisent élevages et cultures, forçant les agriculteurs à trouver des solutions d'urgence pour s’adapter.

france24fr.title: Condamnation de Marine Le Pen : la Cour de cassation se prononcera "au plus tard début avril 2027"
france24fr.description: La Cour de cassation a indiqué mercredi qu'elle devrait pouvoir statuer "au plus tard début avril 2027" sur le pourvoi de Marine Le Pen contre sa condamnation dans l'affaire des assistants d'eurodéputés du Front national (FN, ancêtre du RN). La Cour a toutefois prévenu que ce délai est assujetti à des "facteurs procéduraux".

france24fr.title: Tour de France, cinquième étape : le Néerlandais Olav Kooij remporte le sprint à Pau
france24fr.description: Le Néerlandais Olav Kooij a remporté, mercredi, la cinquième étape du Tour de France à Pau, à l'issue d'un sprint chaotique marqué par plusieurs chutes dans le final.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Marine Le Pen en campagne, jour 1
france24fr.description: Au lendemain de son annonce de candidature malgré sa condamnation en appel, Marine Le Pen a lancé sa campagne à La Flèche, aux côtés de Jordan Bardella.

france24fr.title: "La France se réarme", déclare la ministre française des Armées à France 24
france24fr.description: Alors que le 36ᵉ sommet de l'Otan se tient mercredi à Ankara, la ministre française des Armées a accordé un entretien à France 24 avant de se rendre en Turquie. Réarmement de la France, rallonge sur le budget de l'armée, soutien à l'Ukraine… La ministre a passé en revue les priorités militaires du pays.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi Donald Trump s’entête à vouloir vendre des F-35 à la Turquie
france24fr.description: En dépit de l'opposition du Congrès américain et d'Israël, Donald Trump a annoncé qu’il était temps de revenir sur l’interdiction de la vente des chasseurs F-35 à la Turquie. Car le président des États-Unis veut faire plaisir à Recep Tayyip Erdogan, qu'il considère comme l’un de ses "alliés les plus loyaux".

france24fr.title: Condamnée, Marine Le Pen se pourvoit en cassation et reste candidate à l'Elysée
france24fr.description: La ⁠cheffe de ​file du Rassemblement national (RN), Marine Le ​Pen, a annoncé mardi sur TF1 qu'elle se pourvoyait en cassation après sa condamnation pour ​détournement ‌de fonds publics par ⁠la cour d'appel de Paris et qu'elle restait ‌candidate à l'élection présidentielle de 2027. Les explications de Maître Sandra Chirac Kollarik, avocate de Marine Le Pen.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump menace l’Iran de frappes "fortes" dans la nuit
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a affirmé mercredi que les Etats-Unis allaient frapper "fort" l'Iran cette nuit, à l'issue du sommet de l'Otan à Ankara. "Nous allons les frapper fort cette nuit", a déclaré le président américain devant la presse, interrogé sur la reprise des frappes américaines contre l'Iran.

france24fr.title: Yarn Bombing : quand le tricot devient graffiti
france24fr.description: Le tricot, un truc de grand-mère ? En 2005, un nouvel art urbain est né : le yarn bombing, qui consiste à "taguer" les murs avec du fil. Au-delà de l'aspect esthétique, c'est aussi un moyen pour les femmes d'investir l'espace public. Attendez la fin de la vidéo pour voir le résultat.. #crochet #tricot #knitting

france24fr.title: REPLAY - Trump et Al-Charaa : la Syrie et Israël au cœur des échanges
france24fr.description: Le président syrien Ahmed Al-Charaa et le président américain Donald Trump ont pris la parole en marge du sommet de l'#Otan à Ankara en Turquie. Donald Trump s'est dit prêt à retirer la Syrie de la liste commanditaire du terrorisme.

france24fr.title: Otan : un sommet existentiel ? Parlons-en avec M. Pierini, P. Martin-Genier, C. Bret et A. May
france24fr.description: Deuxième jour du sommet de l'Otan à Ankara. Au programme, photo de famille puis réunion de travail entre les 32 membres de l'Alliance. Donald Trump n'en finit plus d'évoquer la déception que ses alliés lui inspirent à l'exception du président turc, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. Ambiance sur fond de menace de désengagement militaire américain du sol européen. Vit-on un sommet quasi existentiel pour l'Otan ? Les menaces américaines sont-elles de nature à accélérer le serpent de mer de la défense européenn

france24fr.title: REPLAY - Ukraine, Iran : Trump et Zelensky s’expriment au sommet de l’OTAN
france24fr.description: Les Etats-Unis vont frapper "fort" l'Iran cette nuit, a prévenu mercredi le président Donald Trump qui a estimé que le cessez-le-feu était terminé après de violents échanges de frappes, tout en laissant la porte ouverte à la poursuite des tractations avec Téhéran.

france24fr.title: Au sommet de l’OTAN, Trump se défoule contre les alliés européens
france24fr.description: "Je suis très en colère contre l'Otan": Donald Trump a exprimé mercredi sa frustration vis-à-vis de l'Alliance atlantique au dernier jour du sommet d'Ankara, dénonçant, pêle-mêle, l'attitude des alliés sur l'Iran et le Groenland ou l'Espagne.

france24fr.title: Élection présidentielle 2027 : Marine Le Pen candidate
france24fr.description: Marine Le Pen éligible mais condamnée en appel à trois ans de prison dont un an ferme sous bracelet électronique. La cheffe de file des députés RN a, malgré cette condamnation, annoncé être candidate pour 2027. Elle se pourvoit en cassation, ce qui suspend la peine à laquelle elle a été condamnée mais qui la plonge dans un flou juridique. La voie choisit par la leader d'extrême est-elle risquée ? Roselyne Febvre pose la question à Pablo Pillaud-Vivien et Dominique de Montvalon.

france24fr.title: Otan : Donald Trump veut maintenir les États-Unis au sein de l’Alliance
france24fr.description: Donald ​Trump a déclaré mercredi lors du sommet de ​l'Otan qu'il souhaitait que les États-Unis restent au sein de l'alliance transatlantique, a indiqué à Reuters ​une ‌source au fait des ⁠discussions.

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis vont autoriser l'Ukraine à fabriquer des missiles Patriot
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a indiqué mercredi qu'il allait autoriser Kiev à fabriquer des missiles Patriot, indispensables pour intercepter les missiles balistiques russes qui frappent l'Ukraine, lors de sa rencontre avec Volodymyr Zelensky.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : Trump juge la trêve avec l’Iran "terminée"
france24fr.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a affirmé mercredi à Ankara que le cessez-le-feu avec l'Iran était "terminé", ouvrant toutefois la porte à une reprise éventuelle des discussions.

france24fr.title: "Le passage" : Omar Sy dans la peau d'un passeur de migrants
france24fr.description: Au programme de ce numéro 100 % cinéma de "À l'Affiche !" : "Le passage" de l'Américain Brandt Andersen. Ce film choral revient sur la crise migratoire et plus particulièrement sur le sort des migrants syriens obligés de fuir la guerre civile. Filmé comme un thriller, il suit le parcours d'un médecin, d'un soldat mais aussi d'un passeur incarné par Omar Sy.

nzz.title: Mutmassliche Amoktat in Bayern: zwei Schwerverletzte an Gymnasium in Schongau
nzz.description: Die Polizei hat den mutmasslichen Täter festgenommen. Die Opfer verletzte er mit einem Messer. Zudem trug er eine Schusswaffe auf sich.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Nato-Gipfel in Ankara: Bündnis-Chef Rutte kündigt Milliardenprojekt für Treibstoffversorgung an +++ Zusage für neue Militärhilfe für die Ukraine
nzz.description: Die Verteidigungsallianz hat turbulente Monate hinter sich. In Ankara steht ein entscheidendes Treffen an. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Kandidatin mit Fussfessel: Marine Le Pen will trotz Verurteilung erneut für das Präsidentenamt kandidieren
nzz.description: Die französische Justiz hat Marine Le Pen wegen der Veruntreuung öffentlicher Gelder schuldig gesprochen – aber ihre Strafe deutlich gemildert. Die Frontfrau des Rassemblement national kündigte am Dienstagabend eine vierte Kandidatur für den Élysée-Palast an.

nzz.title: Der Schwarm der Schwimmer: 9000 Personen nehmen an der Seeüberquerung teil
nzz.description: Warmes Wetter, beste Bedingungen: An der traditionellen Querung des Zürichsees waren alle Startplätze ausverkauft. Die besten Bilder des Anlasses 2026.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Der Regierende Bürgermeister von Berlin wird seinem Amt nicht gerecht. Er sollte zurücktreten
nzz.description: Kai Wegner hat sich mit seinem Krisenmanagement nicht gerade verausgabt. Schwerer noch wiegt, dass er den Bürgern nicht die Wahrheit darüber gesagt hat.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Drei Tote nach russischem Drohnenangriff in Kiew +++ Trump stellt Selenski Lizenz für Patriot-Produktion in Aussicht
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Das Nato-Treffen in der Türkei in Bildern
nzz.description: Diese Woche treffen sich die Nato-Mitglieder zu ihrem 36. Gipfel, das zweite Mal in der Türkei. US-Präsident Donald Trump und der ukrainische Präsident Wolodimir Selenski sind ebenfalls angereist.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: EU-Abgeordnete fordern Untersuchung gegen Infantino +++ Kroatiens Erfolgscoach Dalic tritt zurück, Martínez-Aus bei Portugal bestätigt
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: Donald Trump erklärt den Waffenstillstand für beendet – und will trotzdem weiterverhandeln
nzz.description: Amerikas Präsident beschimpft Irans Regime als «Abschaum», während sich die Streitkräfte beider Länder einen neuen Schlagabtausch liefern. Dennoch spricht einiges dafür, dass weder Washington noch Teheran den offenen Krieg wollen.

nzz.title: Sudan: Die Angst vor einem Massenmord in al-Obeid wächst
nzz.description: Im Bürgerkriegsland Sudan entwickelt sich die Stadt al-Obeid zu einem neuen Brennpunkt. Für die Menschen wird das Überleben immer schwieriger, weil die RSF-Miliz die Stadt belagern und bombardiert. Experten warnen vor einem Szenario wie in al-Fashir.

nzz.title: Mitten in Manhattan droht ein Hochhaus einzustürzen, Tausende müssen evakuiert werden
nzz.description: Am Dienstag verbogen sich auf der Baustelle im 21. Stock eines Gebäudes in New York plötzlich Stahlträger. Die Stadt reagierte mit einem Grosseinsatz. Das Umbauprojekt hatte schon früher Probleme gemacht.

nzz.title: In Zürich dürfen Public Viewings das Viertelfinalspiel der Schweiz mitten in der Nacht zeigen – und dies, nachdem Parlamentarier solche Anlässe komplett verbieten wollten
nzz.description: Das WM-Spiel der Schweizer Nationalmannschaft fällt mit dem Beginn der «Mediterranen Nächte» in Zürich zusammen. Zürich steht ein lauter Sommer bevor.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Donald Trump, eine Sonnenbrille und eine «lame duck» – was das Gruppenbild über den Nato-Gipfel aussagt
nzz.description: In Ankara treffen sich derzeit die Regierungschefs des Verteidigungsbündnisses. Während sich manche wieder einander annähern, sind andere nicht gut aufeinander zu sprechen.

nzz.title: Zürichs Sozialisten streiten über das Cüpli
nzz.description: Ein Genosse will der eigenen Partei verbieten, Gratisalkohol auszuschenken. Die Parteispitze reagiert kühl.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Cum-Ex-Skandal: Bundesgerichtshof bestätigt Bewährungsstrafe für Kronzeuge Kai-Uwe Steck
nzz.description: Cum-Ex-Aktiengeschäfte haben den Fiskus in Deutschland laut Schätzungen mindestens zehn Milliarden Euro gekostet. Worum geht es beim grössten Steuerskandal der deutschen Nachkriegsgeschichte?

nzz.title: Wiedersehen mit Messi: 2014 verpasste die Schweiz das Fussballwunder – Argentinien will die Sensation erneut verhindern
nzz.description: Im Viertelfinal trifft das Schweizer Team auf den Weltmeister. Für Argentinien ist alles andere als der Titel ein Misserfolg – unverwundbar ist die Mannschaft jedoch nicht.

zeit.title: Tennis in Wimbledon: Zverev dominiert Angstgegner: Zwei Siege zum Triumph
Mögliche Amoktat: Gewalttat am Gymnasium - «Schreckliche Stunden» in Schongau
Irankrieg: So bleibt Trump nichts anderes als Krieg
zeit.description: Wenn USA und Iran ihren vermeintlichen Frieden nun wieder aufgeben, wird vor allem eines sichtbar: Das Regime in Teheran ist eine Gefahr, mit der nicht zu verhandeln ist.

zeit.title: Krisenmanagement: Regierender: Habe mich für Darstellung entschuldigt
Polizeieinsatz in Bayern: Was über die Amoktat von Schongau bekannt ist
zeit.description: In einem Gymnasium in Schongau werden zwei Mädchen mit einem Messer lebensgefährlich verletzt. Die Polizei nimmt einen Jugendlichen fest. Ein Überblick

zeit.title: Wohnen mit Ex-Partner: Sind Sie getrennt, aber wohnen noch zusammen?
zeit.description: Trennungen sind schwer, Wohnungssuche noch mehr. Wir suchen Paare, die Schluss gemacht haben, aber weiter zusammenwohnen. Erzählen Sie uns Ihre Geschichte.

zeit.title: Rettungseinsatz: Kletterer stürzt ab - Rettungshubschrauber im Einsatz
Transfer: Keeper Nübel verlässt den FC Bayern und wechselt zu Besiktas
Reformen der Alpenländer: Huch, eine Reform!
zeit.description: Österreich versucht die Staatsreform, Deutschland ist eine Großbaustelle – und in der Schweiz? Wie unsere Länder umgebaut werden. Außerdem: Was Friseure kosten (sollten).

zeit.title: Tennis: Alexander Zverev zieht ins Wimbledon-Halbfinale ein
zeit.description: Der deutsche Tennisspieler gewann im Viertelfinale gegen Taylor Fritz überraschend glatt. Alexander Zverev steht damit zum ersten Mal im Wimbledon-Halbfinale.

zeit.title: Hessische Landesvertretung: «Hessenfest»: Hessen feiert und präsentiert sich in Berlin
Nato-Gipfel: Donald Trump erwägt neue Angriffe gegen den Iran
zeit.description: Der US-Präsident spricht in Ankara von »Liebe« unter den Nato-Partnern. Eine neue Eskalation im Irankrieg sieht er nicht. »Es wird schnell vorüber sein«, sagte Trump.

zeit.title: Wohnungsbau: Wir müssen endlich wieder einfacher bauen!
zeit.description: Barrierefreiheit, Energieeffizienz, Schallschutz: Deutschland setzt auf absurd hohe Standards und bremst so den Wohnungsbau. Es ginge deutlich einfacher und günstiger.

observador.title: Novas regras para passageiros nos voos. "Acordo não é per...
observador.description: O Parlamento Europeu aprovou novas regras de proteção aos passageiros. O eurodeputado Sérgio Humberto fala da mochila grátis, o fim de taxas surpresa e o direito ao bilhete em papel a partir de 2027.

observador.title: As notícias das 18h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Portugal regista 237 mortes em excesso durante onda de calor
observador.description: País registou excesso de mortalidade durante pelo menos quatro dias, até esta terça-feira. INEM e linha SNS registam elevada procura, mas pressão nas urgências ainda não é significativa.

observador.title: Agualva-Cacém. Sintra vai apoiar famílias das vítimas
observador.description: A família de uma das vítimas mortais já era acompanhada por uma junta de freguesia. Autarquia enviou cinco pessoas para o local.

observador.title: Almada em situação de alerta devido aos cortes de água
observador.description: Câmara esteve reunida com entidade reguladora e com a APA e decidiu reforço das "equipas técnicas para a deteção e reparação urgente de fugas e roturas".

observador.title: NOS Alive 2026: 15 concertos a não perder
observador.description: Os regressos dos Foo Fighters e de Nick Cave; a estreia de Teddy Swims; o fenómeno Zara Larsson; o acontecimento que é o concerto dos Buraka Som Sistema. O festival está de volta, de 9 a 11 de julho.

observador.title: Grupo lucrou milhões com regularização ilegal de migrantes
observador.description: Operação "Neblina Atlântica" desmantelou grupo que cobrava 200 euros por processo e lucrou milhões. A maioria das vítimas vive na Bélgica, França e Suíça.

observador.title: Educação refém dos fundos europeus, diz ministro
observador.description: Fernando Alexandre acusou governos anteriores de definir escolas e cursos profissionais conforme os fundos disponíveis, não as necessidades. CTeSP vão ganhar novo estatuto legal.

observador.title: Rússia proíbe exportações de gasóleo por pouco combustível
observador.description: Com esta medida, a oferta do mercado interno vai aumentar. A decisão surge como forma de responder às perturbações no abastecimento de combustíveis, agravadas pelos ataques ucranianos.

observador.title: Farage vai a votos em agosto sem principais rivais
observador.description: Líder do Reform UK vai a votos em Clacton-on-Sea, depois de investigações sobre irregularidades financeiras. Partidos anunciam boicote à eleição parlamentar parcial.

observador.title: Prisão de líder do PAIGC pode levar a "guerra civil"
observador.description: Rosto da oposição guineense ouvido várias horas no Tribunal Militar para decidir sobre a sua prisão preventiva. Sociedade civil reagiu: se Domingos Simões Pereira for preso, pode haver guerra civil.

observador.title: Imprensa egípcia critica arbitragem do jogo com a Argentina
observador.description: Imprensa egípcia faz acusações ao árbitro e ao VAR do encontro entre Egito e Argentina. Suspeitas de ligações entre as direções desportivas e instituições financeiras também são referidas.

observador.title: Assédio sexual. Militar americano evita julgamento britânico
observador.description: Hannes Marschalek foi julgado num tribunal militar nos EUA e chegou a acordo judicial. Caso tivesse sido julgado no Reino Unido, poderia ter enfrentado uma pena de prisão de até dois anos.

observador.title: Fraude fiscal nos combustíveis custa 460 milhões ao Estado
observador.description: O prejuízo decorre de esquemas no imposto petrolífero e no IVA. O Governo já aprovou várias medidas para travar o avanço destas infrações, mas a implementação no terreno ainda vai demorar.

observador.title: Efeitos colaterais do calor, crédito aperta e a fraude cara
observador.description: Calor extremo afeta trabalhadores, comboios e até o abastecimento de água em Almada. Aperto no crédito à habitação em agosto. Estado perde centenas de milhões nos combustíveis. E a Easyjet na mira.

observador.title: IHRU. Leilão de imóveis não é "mau negócio" para o Estado
observador.description: O presidente do IHRU rejeita que o Estado esteja a vender imóveis abaixo do preço de mercado. No parlamento, Benjamim Pereira elogiou o trabalho do Governo na habitação.

observador.title: Sismos. Caracas quer fundos congelados para reconstrução
observador.description: Ministro dos Negócios Estrangeiros apelou à libertação de contas do Estado bloqueadas no estrangeiro. EUA já suspenderam sanções por quatro meses após duplo sismo de 24 de junho.

observador.title: Condenado a 15 anos por abuso sexual de menores
observador.description: O homem foi acusado de 41 crimes de abuso sexual de menores. Para além da condenação a prisão efetiva, está também proibido de exercer profissões que envolvam contactos com menores.

spiegel.title: Nato-Gipfel in Ankara: Hat Donald Trump das Bündnis bereits abgehakt?
spiegel.description: Beim Nato-Gipfel in Ankara droht Donald Trump den Dänen und kanzelt die Spanier ab, das Bündnis hat er anscheinend bereits abgehakt. Doch hinter verschlossenen Türen, so heißt es, soll es anders gelaufen sein.

spiegel.title: Österreich: Urteil gegen Hotelmanager wegen Burkini-Verbot
spiegel.description: Ein Hotel verbietet zwei Österreicherinnen, Ganzkörper-Schwimmanzüge zu tragen – angeblich aus hygienischen Gründen. Jetzt entscheidet ein Gericht, das Verbot ist diskriminierend.

spiegel.title: Landgericht Berlin: Mediziner gab Tipps zur Vergewaltigung von Frauen – fünf Jahre Haft
spiegel.description: Ein Mediziner aus China gab in einer Chatgruppe Tipps zur Sedierung von Frauen. Laut Gericht wurde ein empfohlenes Mittel bei mindestens einer späteren Vergewaltigung genutzt. Er wurde nun wegen Beihilfe verurteilt.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Warum die Bahn eine gemeinsame App für alle Anbieter boykottiert
spiegel.description: Eine einzige App für alle Zuganbieter: Darauf hat Verkehrsminister Schnieder Hoffnung gemacht. Doch die Deutsche Bahn boykottiert das Vorhaben.

spiegel.title: Commerzbank-Übernahme durch UniCredit: Mailänder Bank lässt Fahrplan offen
spiegel.description: Die UniCredit ist der feindlichen Übernahme der Commerzbank einen großen Schritt näher. Doch den weiteren Fahrplan lässt die Mailänder Bank offen. In Frankfurt machen sich die ersten Mitarbeiter offenbar schon auf alles gefasst.

spiegel.title: Fahrradkuriere bauen im Schnitt fast einen Unfall pro Jahr
spiegel.description: Sie sind aus dem öffentlichen Raum kaum mehr wegzudenken: Kuriere, die mit Fahrrädern Essen, Lebensmittel und Waren transportieren. Jetzt belegt eine Studie, sie seien bei ihrer Arbeit einem hohen Risiko ausgesetzt.

spiegel.title: Die Dixi-Klos an den Grenzen bleiben – die Kontrollen der Bundespolizei auch?
spiegel.description: Der Polizeibeauftragte des Bundes warnt in seinem Jahresbericht angesichts der Grenzkontrollen vor einer Überforderung der Bundespolizei. Auch die EU dringt auf ein Ende. Und Innenminister Alexander Dobrindt?

spiegel.title: China: Fluten spülen mehr als 900 Giftschlangen aus Gehegen
spiegel.description: Sie recken ihre Köpfe aus dem braunen Wasser: In der Region Guangxi in China sind bei Hochwasser Hunderte Schlangen ins Freie gespült worden. Anwohner wehren sich brachial gegen die Tiere.

spiegel.title: Niedersachsen: Bund bürgt für Milliardenauftrag an Meyer Werft
spiegel.description: Die Unterschrift unter der Kreuzfahrtschiff-Bestellung von MSC Cruises in Papenburg fehlt weiterhin. Nun gewährt der Bund Garantien für das Geschäft, das bis zu zehn Milliarden Euro in die Kasse der Werft spülen könnte.

spiegel.title: Wimbledon: Alexander Zverev schlägt Angstgegner Taylor Fritz – im Halbfinale wartet ein Außenseiter
spiegel.description: Siebenmal in Folge hatte Alexander Zverev gegen Taylor Fritz das Nachsehen, im Wimbledon-Viertelfinale gewann der Deutsche glatt in drei Sätzen. Im Halbfinale trifft er auf den absoluten Publikumsliebling des Turniers.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Polizisten neun Jahre nach G20-Gipfel verurteilt
spiegel.description: Weil sie 2017 während der G20-Proteste einen jungen Mann mit Schlagstöcken und Fäusten traktierten, wurden Polizisten nun erstmals zu Geldstrafen verurteilt. Zwei Angeklagte boten dem Opfer zusätzlich Schmerzensgeld an.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz schwärmt von Nato-Zusammenhalt und lobt Donald Trump
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident hat das Nato-Treffen mit Kritik an den Mitgliedstaaten aufgemischt. Kanzler Merz findet trotzdem anerkennende Worte für Trump. Das Ergebnis des Gipfels spreche für ihn.

spiegel.title: 5. Etappe der Tour de France: Olav Kooij gewinnt den Sprint in Pau
spiegel.description: Die Tour de France hält nach einer halben Woche den ersten Tag für die Sprinter parat. Spezialist Olav Kooij lässt sich das nicht entgehen. Das Gelbe Trikot bleibt ungefährdet.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Marine Le Pen stellt sich über Urteil und provoziert Rechtsstaat – SPIEGEL-Leitartikel
spiegel.description: Marine Le Pen wird des Millionenbetrugs schuldig gesprochen – und will doch Staatspräsidentin werden. Frankreichs rechte Frontfrau fordert den demokratischen Rechtsstaat heraus.

spiegel.title: Markus Braun: Früherer Wirecard-Boss klagt über Trennung von seiner Familie
spiegel.description: Sechs Jahre sitzt der einstige Börsenstar Markus Braun bereits in Untersuchungshaft. Schwierig sei, aus dem Familienleben »herausgerissen« zu sein. Wann ein Urteil im Milliardenbetrugsprozess gegen ihn fällt, ist unklar.

spiegel.title: »Tagesschau«: Sprecherin Susanne Daubner lädt Elmo aus der »Sesamstraße« in ihre letzte Sendung ein
spiegel.description: Gelacht wird eher selten in der »Tagesschau«. In Susanne Daubners letzter Sendung könnte es so weit sein: Die Sprecherin hofft auf einen Besuch von Elmo aus der »Sesamstraße«.

spiegel.title: IOC entscheidet über Russlands Rückkehr in den Weltsport: Das Salami-Komitee

new-sci.description: We used to think post-menopausal ovaries sat inert in the body, but evidence from mice suggests they may instead turn into an organ with a role in inflammation

new-sci.title: Bumblebee facial movements give clues to their inner lives
new-sci.description: A series of experiments shows that bees respond differently to tastes depending on their internal states, hinting that they have something akin to our emotions

new-sci.title: Artefacts hint at cultural exchange between Neanderthals and humans
new-sci.description: A cave on the Turkish Mediterranean coast was inhabited first by Neanderthals and then Homo sapiens, but the continuity of tools and personal objects suggests there was some sharing of culture between the two species

new-sci.title: How healthy is your brain? We now know how to find out
new-sci.description: In our efforts to keep our brains healthy, how do we know what is working? Helen Thomson explores a new generation of tests that can reveal whether our efforts are paying off

new-sci.title: 5 things to know about sunscreen, according to a skin cancer expert
new-sci.description: How much sunscreen should you be using, when should you apply it, and are there any downsides to doing so? Skin cancer expert Rachel Neale is here to answer all of these questions and more

new-sci.title: Musical take on The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind is moving and charming
new-sci.description: A TED talk and then a film, William Kamkwamba’s story of how he worked to provide his rural Malawian village with electricity has now been turned into a musical – and it mostly works, says Bethan Ackerley

new-sci.title: Human brains may have got bigger for no particular reason
new-sci.description: Our brains are large compared with other animals, so it is tempting to assume there was an evolutionary advantage to them – but that may not be true at all

phys-org.title: Employees who feel overqualified view more work tasks as unreasonable
phys-org.description: Employers typically seek out well-qualified candidates, but a new study by researchers in the Penn State School of Hospitality Management highlights the potential risks associated with workers who feel overqualified for their jobs. When employees saw themselves as overqualified, they were more likely to consider some of their workload unfair or worthless, the researchers said.

phys-org.title: Simple treatment strengthens pineapple leaf fibers for sustainable composites
phys-org.description: Pineapple leaf fiber has long been valued in parts of Southeast Asia for traditional uses, including basketry in Malaysia and Thailand and textile applications in the Philippines. Its high cellulose content and ready availability as an agricultural residue have also made it attractive as a reinforcement for polymer composites.

phys-org.title: Study explores social media's role in tornado disaster communication
phys-org.description: When a powerful EF-4 tornado tore through Rolling Fork, Mississippi, on March 24, 2023, social media became a critical tool for sharing weather warnings, damage reports and recovery information. But a new study from University of Nebraska–Lincoln media scholar Cory Armstrong found that the same disaster also exposed persistent communication gaps facing rural and underserved communities.

phys-org.title: Is the state of nature fair? Researchers measure how biomass is distributed in microbial communities
phys-org.description: The distribution of income and growing inequality are central themes in public debate. Far less attention has been paid to how resources are distributed in ecological communities, in the so-called state of nature, without any social contract. Species abundance distributions have been studied extensively in ecology, but descriptively. They largely follow a distribution similar to human wealth. Yet the fairness of that distribution has rarely been examined.

phys-org.title: What powers the Everglades? Study tracks how algae and plant matter fuel the food web
phys-org.description: Scientists thought dead plant material was primarily powering the Everglades. Algae says not so fast.

phys-org.title: How do World Cup crowds get synchronized so quickly? Researchers explain
phys-org.description: Some World Cup crowds are more in sync than others, but all have some common features, Northeastern experts say.

phys-org.title: Traveling protein waves reveal how dividing cells set chromosome-splitting spindle size
phys-org.description: When a human cell prepares to split into two daughter cells, it must first construct a tiny internal machine called the mitotic spindle—a structure of protein fibers that physically pulls chromosomes apart and deposits one set into each new cell. Get the spindle the right size and the chromosomes segregate cleanly. Getting it wrong could result in the chromosomal errors that fuel cancer.

phys-org.title: From the lab to the moon: Lunar cement alternative survives 6 months on ISS and returned stronger in some tests
phys-org.description: Building material samples from the University of Delaware spent six months mounted outside the International Space Station, where the harsh conditions of low Earth orbit tested their limits.

phys-org.title: How cells keep genomic hitchhikers under control
phys-org.description: Much of the genome is made up of repetitive DNA sequences that trace back to ancient mobile elements, many of which have lost their ability to copy themselves into new locations but can still cause problems if they become active again at the wrong time. Now, two studies published in Molecular Cell from FMI scientists reveal how cells keep these potentially disruptive genetic elements under control. The researchers found that a protein complex called ChAHP acts as a targeted genome-defense system

phys-org.description: More than 90% of the key nutrients degrading the Mar Menor, such as ammonium, phosphorus and silica, do not come from streams or continental groundwater, but rather through a mechanism that has so far been overlooked: Water from the lagoon itself infiltrates the sediments and re-emerges loaded with nutrients that have accumulated over years. phys-org.title: Making the 'invisible' visible: How high-speed movies could change the way scientists study disease
phys-org.description: High-speed movies of microscopic worms may sound like a dull night at the cinema, but this advanced imaging capability could help scientists better understand how diseases begin and progress, track subtle changes in cells and study how the body responds to treatments.

phys-org.title: Nanoplastics found in Antarctic soils for first time, suggesting long-range atmospheric transport
phys-org.description: Microplastic contamination has been a much-discussed topic over the last several years, but contamination from even smaller plastic particles represents another pressing issue. Nanoplastics—defined as being under a micrometer in diameter—may pose an even higher ecological risk because they can travel more easily, cross cellular membranes and easily adsorb other pollutants.

phys-org.title: Turning up the heat on cancer: Manganese ferrite nanoparticles outperform rivals
phys-org.description: Scientists have long known that heat can be used to help fight cancer. But heating tumors and cancer cells is trickier than it sounds. Apply too much heat and patients could get hurt; apply too little or target the wrong location and the therapy will not be effective.

phys-org.title: Large language model guides discovery of catalysts for clean energy tech
phys-org.description: Designing high-performance catalysts is essential for cleaner energy technologies, but the behavior of multi-element modern catalyst materials is difficult to predict. In a new study, researchers at Tohoku University with international collaborators developed a collaborative framework that combines large language models with lab experiments to accelerate the discovery of high-entropy alloy catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction, a key process in fuel cells.

phys-org.title: Tiny 60,000-neuron ant brains reveal how parental care evolved from feeding circuits
phys-org.description: Long before the dawn of modern parenting, animals laid eggs and moved on, leaving their progeny to fend for themselves. Now, a study published in Nature uncovers one of the elegant ways evolution transformed neglect into nurture. Working with clonal raider ants, a surprisingly parental insect, researchers found that rather than evolving entirely new brain circuits for caregiving, evolution repurposed ancient neural systems for regulating hunger into triggers for social behaviors.

phys-org.title: A hotter climate may lead to more same-sex mounting in corpse-eating beetles
phys-org.description: New research suggests that heat stress increases the occurrence of same-sex sexual interactions between male burying beetles—but also that a surprising number of male–male encounters occur under control conditions. This ongoing project is investigating whether a possible trade-off between heat protection and social-communication cuticular hydrocarbons may be involved in possible sex-recognition errors, and whether these behaviors may result in any costs to reproductive success.

phys-org.title: In time but out of tune: Exploring the rapid evolution of Hawaii's songless crickets
phys-org.description: New research finds that the "silent" mutant male crickets of Hawaii, first observed more than 20 years ago, have now become well established across the Hawaiian islands, and that the reproductive challenges caused by a lack of courtship song may be offset by much earlier maturation into adulthood, providing a wider window for breeding opportunities. phys-org.description: An ongoing research project exploring the effects of rising levels of oceanic CO2 on squid neurology reveals that exposure to future levels of ocean acidification could shrink their brain volume by around 50%. This severe brain shrinkage appears to be most pronounced in the areas that interpret visual information, correlating with significant reductions in normal feeding behaviors and suggesting serious consequences for the future of squid and other cephalopods.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: How Argentina Can Protect Its Resource Wealth
proj-syn.description: Alaska, Norway, and Chile recognized the economic and political risks that accompany commodity booms and established sovereign wealth funds to preserve their resource revenues. Argentina’s hydrocarbon- and lithium-rich provinces should learn from their experience.

proj-syn.title: Reinventing Development Finance
proj-syn.description: Faced with shrinking concessional finance and rising borrowing costs, Rwanda has worked with the World Bank Group to leverage limited public funds and risk-sharing instruments to unlock private capital at scale and on affordable terms. It's an arrangement holding important lessons for low-income countries that must do more with less.

proj-syn.title: Mamdani’s American Dream
proj-syn.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Independence Day address was a perfect example of ideology in the positive sense of the term. It overturned both the right-wing populist narrative of the United States and the left-wing "woke" critique with a vision that has the potential to mobilize a majority.

proj-syn.title: How Vulnerable Are US Financial Markets?
proj-syn.description: Fueled by more than $1 trillion in borrowed money and rising leverage across the financial system, US stock markets may have entered bubble territory. Two developments could trigger a sharp correction: higher interest rates and a loss of confidence in the handful of tech giants driving the AI boom.

proj-syn.title: Concessional Finance Is Needed More Than Ever
proj-syn.description: As debt burdens rise and climate shocks intensify, sustainable financing mechanisms are becoming indispensable. The Islamic Development Bank’s new concessional fund offers a promising model for mobilizing the resources needed to protect development gains and invest in resilience.

proj-syn.title: Ruling Class Clowns
proj-syn.description: By the end of the 19th-century in the US, it was clear to all interested observers that market power did not automatically or even easily translate into political capital and cultural authority. That is why, unlike the oligarchs of our time, certain Gilded Age capitalists learned how to become a ruling class.

proj-syn.title: The Missing Ingredient for European Tech Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: Europe’s dependence on US technology companies is both an economic challenge and a strategic vulnerability. The European Union’s new Tech Sovereignty Package is a step in the right direction, but without equally ambitious efforts to curb market concentration, it is bound to fall short.

proj-syn.title: In Praise of the World Cup’s Little Guys
proj-syn.description: In a world of great-power rivalry and hyper-scaling tech behemoths, you would be forgiven for thinking that the bulky bully always has the edge. But as this year's World Cup has shown repeatedly, you would be wrong.

proj-syn.title: Inside Ukraine’s Game-Changing Drone Industry
proj-syn.description: In recent months, Ukrainian drones have successfully struck dozens of sites deep inside Russia, targeting the oil industry, weapons plants, and logistics hubs. But while Ukraine has developed a world-leading military technology to defend itself from a much larger aggressor, drones will not be enough to end the war.

proj-syn.title: Just Say No to Remote Work
proj-syn.description: Even during the immediate post-pandemic period, when evidence on the labor-market effects of remote work was scant, there was a strong case to be made for going into the office, especially for younger workers. And now, multiple new studies have vindicated this intuition.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Acceptable Path for Designer Babies
proj-syn.description: Genetic-engineering tools with which to design one's progeny already exist, and they are being made even more potent with AI—at least for those who can afford such services. In the absence of policy interventions, we will be hurtling toward a tiered society in which economic privileges become biological advantages.

proj-syn.title: The Democratic Turkey NATO Needs
proj-syn.description: At NATO's upcoming summit in Ankara, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will seek to portray his country as stable, confident, and essential to Western security. But only the last one is true, which is why the restoration of democracy in Turkey is more than a domestic concern.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup as It Should Be
proj-syn.description: While Donald Trump was widely expected to lord over this year’s World Cup, which the United States is co-hosting with Mexico and Canada, it has turned out not to be his scene. National teams populated with immigrants, and small-town America’s embrace of the event, go against everything Trump’s MAGA movement stands for.

proj-syn.title: The Real Threat to NATO
proj-syn.description: The greatest challenge to NATO comes not from its adversaries but from within. As its leaders gather in Ankara on July 7-8, they should focus less on military capabilities than on reinvigorating the alliance's founding strategic philosophy, centered on democratic legitimacy, human rights, and the rule of law.

proj-syn.title: How the EU Can Lead the Rest of the West
proj-syn.description: While Europe is not just another middle power, nor is it a great power with sufficient economic, military, and geopolitical clout to dictate terms on the global stage. Instead, Europe is the ideal candidate to convene and lead a group of like-minded middle powers, not as a US-style hegemon, but as a first among equals.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Face the World on Its Own
proj-syn.description: Under pressure from Russian aggression—which has reached its full expression in the ongoing war against Ukraine—and an increasingly hostile US administration, Europe urgently needs to make progress toward a defense union. But that will require Franco-German leadership of the kind that is not yet on offer.

proj-syn.title: How Safe Are Today’s Blockbuster Tech Stocks?
proj-syn.description: Today’s wave of mega-IPOs has unleashed a wave of analogies to past booms. While no analogy is perfect, an especially apposite—and sobering—case may be what followed Nippon Telegraph and Telephone’s IPO in February 1987.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dolce Vita?
proj-syn.description: Glacial growth, aging welfare states, and a shortage of centrist leaders suggest Europe faces a major debt crisis in the years ahead. But its emphasis on leisure over work could become a decisive advantage, positioning the continent as the leading model for thriving in an age of AI-driven abundance.
